subject: Business
title: The Suez Canal Blockage: A Case Study
description: A fast breakdown of The Suez Canal Blockage: A Case Study for builders.

hook.text: In 2021, one ship got stuck sideways in the Suez Canal. Global trade lost $9.6 billion per day for six days.

buildup.text: The Ever Given, one of the world's largest container ships, was wedged across the canal by wind and a navigation error.

discovery.text: 12% of global trade passes through the Suez Canal. Blocking it created a traffic jam of 400+ ships.

twist.text: The ripple effects lasted months. Ports were congested, schedules scrambled, and container shortages worsened globally.

climax.text: The lesson: one chokepoint in a global system can cascade into disruption that costs billions and lasts months.

punchline.text: The global economy can be held hostage by a single stuck ship.

quiz.question: How much trade passes through the Suez Canal?

details.summary: In March 2021, the container ship Ever Given ran aground in the Suez Canal, blocking the waterway for six days and halting an estimated 9.6 billion dollars of daily trade. The incident exposed how a single chokepoint failure can cascade through global supply chains.
details.whyItMatters: The Suez blockage demonstrated that global supply chains depend on a few critical chokepoints. A single stuck ship disrupted trade routes handling 12 percent of global commerce, delaying shipments for months afterward.
takeaways: The Ever Given blocked the Suez Canal for six days in March 2021
An estimated 9.6 billion dollars in daily trade was disrupted
Chokepoint vulnerabilities reveal systemic risk in global shipping routes

faq.question: What caused the Ever Given to block the Suez Canal?
faq.answer: High winds and a sandstorm caused the 400-meter ship to lose steering and run aground diagonally across the canal. Its enormous size made it impossible to pass, and freeing it required dredging, tugboats, and favorable tidal conditions over six days.

faq.question: What were the lasting impacts beyond the six-day blockage?
faq.answer: Over 400 ships were delayed, creating port congestion for months afterward. Shipping schedules and container availability were disrupted globally. Companies accelerated investments in supply chain visibility and diversified routing. Insurance and canal transit costs increased.
